issues.legal_issue: A notice to terminate a monthly tenancy is valid when, construed in a common-sense manner, it makes clear that the tenant may remain until the end of the tenancy month and that the tenancy ends only then.
material_facts: The tenancy was a monthly tenancy.
The notice required the tenants to vacate within October and said they would be treated as trespassers from 1 November if they did not do so.
The notice was given on 25 September, and the stated date for treating the tenants as trespassers was after the end of October.
issues.conclusion: The notice was valid and determined the tenancy with effect from the end of 31 October.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, a monthly tenancy must be terminated by notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy. A notice to quit is construed ut res magis valeat quam pereat, in a common-sense rather than hyper-critical manner. Applying Sidebotham v. Holland and Harihar Banerji v. Ramsashi Roy, the Court held that requiring vacation within the month, while stating that the tenants would be trespassers from the first day of the next month, showed that the tenancy ended only at the month's end.

predicates.monthly_tenancy_notice_challenge: The proceeding challenges whether a notice validly terminates a monthly tenancy.
predicates.notice_allows_occupancy_through_month_en: The notice permits the tenant to remain in possession through the end of the tenancy month.
predicates.trespasser_status_begins_next_month: The notice states that the tenant will be treated as a trespasser beginning only in the month after the stated tenancy month.

issues.definition: When a notice in a challenge concerning a monthly tenancy permits occupation through the end of the month and places trespasser status in the following month, the notice validly terminates the tenancy at month-end.
